Upstream's OpenGL renderer

Source: R/zz_opengl_renderer.R, R/zz_opengl_software.R
opengl_renderer.Rd

Upstream's OpenGL renderer keeps a camera mobject, a tree of 3D objects and meshes, and compiled shader programs, and draws them with moderngl. manimR computes what upstream computes on the CPU and draws the result in software, with a context whose framebuffers are off screen graphics devices:

Usage

OpenGLCamera(
  frame_shape = NULL,
  center_point = NULL,
  euler_angles = NULL,
  focal_distance = 2,
  light_source_position = NULL,
  orthographic = FALSE,
  minimum_polar_angle = -PI/2,
  maximum_polar_angle = PI/2,
  model_matrix = NULL,
  ...
)

Object3D(...)

Mesh(
  shader = NULL,
  attributes = NULL,
  geometry = NULL,
  material = NULL,
  indices = NULL,
  use_depth_test = TRUE,
  primitive = 4L
)

Shader(context = NULL, name = NULL, source = NULL)

FullScreenQuad(
  context = NULL,
  fragment_shader_source = NULL,
  fragment_shader_name = NULL
)

filter_attributes(unfiltered_attributes, attributes)

build_matrix_lists(mob)

triangulate_mobject(mob)

affects_shader_info_id(func)

triggers_refreshed_triangulation(func)

OpenGLSoftwareContext(...)

render_opengl_vectorized_mobject_fill(renderer, mobject)

render_mobject_fills_with_matrix(renderer, model_matrix, mobjects)

render_opengl_vectorized_mobject_stroke(renderer, mobject)

render_mobject_strokes_with_matrix(renderer, model_matrix, mobjects)

OpenGLRenderer(
  file_writer_class = SceneFileWriterClass,
  skip_animations = FALSE
)

Window(
  renderer,
  window_size = cfg("window_size"),
  monitor = NULL,
  open = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

frame_shape

Width and height of the frame; the config's frame size by default.

center_point

Center of the frame.

euler_angles

theta, phi and gamma, in radians.

focal_distance

Focal distance, in frame heights.

light_source_position

Position of the light.

orthographic

Whether the projection is orthographic.

minimum_polar_angle, maximum_polar_angle

Limits of phi.

model_matrix

Initial model matrix.

...

For OpenGLCamera(), further arguments for OpenGLMobject(); for Object3D(), child objects.

shader, material

A Shader.

attributes

For Mesh(), shader data (see ShaderWrapper()); for filter_attributes(), the names of the attributes to keep.

geometry

A mesh whose attributes and indices are used.

indices

Vertex indices, 0 based.

use_depth_test

Whether the mesh is drawn with a depth test.

primitive

moderngl primitive number (4 for triangles).

context

A context, as OpenGLSoftwareContext(), kept with the shader.

name

Name of a shader folder under SHADER_FOLDER.

source

List of GLSL code.

fragment_shader_source, fragment_shader_name

Code of the fragment shader, or the name of a .frag file under SHADER_FOLDER.

unfiltered_attributes

Shader data.

mob

An OpenGL mobject.

func

A method, a function of self and further arguments.

renderer

An OpenGLRenderer.

mobject

An OpenGL VMobject.

mobjects

A list of OpenGL VMobjects.

file_writer_class

Class of the scene's file writer.

skip_animations

Whether animations are skipped.

window_size

"default", "width,height" or two integers.

monitor

List of x, y, width and height of the monitor.

open

Whether to open the window's graphics device.

Value

OpenGLCamera(), Object3D(), Mesh(), Shader(), FullScreenQuad(), OpenGLRenderer(), OpenGLSoftwareContext() and Window() return R6 objects; the render_* functions return NULL invisibly; filter_attributes() and triangulate_mobject() shader data; build_matrix_lists() a list of mobject lists named by the 16 values of their matrix, row by row; the decorators a function.

Details

  • OpenGLCamera() is upstream's camera mobject: a frame of five points (center, left, right, bottom, top), a model matrix that places it at (0, 0, 11), Euler angles (theta, phi, gamma) and the projection and view matrices.

  • Object3D(...) is a node of a tree of objects with a model matrix, a normal matrix and updaters; Mesh() adds vertex attributes, indices and a shader, and FullScreenQuad() is a mesh covering the frame. Mesh$render() needs an OpenGL context and stops.

  • Shader(context, name, source) reads the GLSL code of a shader folder under SHADER_FOLDER (or takes source, a list of vertex_shader, fragment_shader and geometry_shader code) and keeps it in shader_program_cache by name; set_uniform() stores a value for a uniform the code declares and ignores others, as upstream.

  • filter_attributes() keeps the named attributes of shader data.

  • build_matrix_lists() groups a mobject's family by hierarchical model matrix, and triangulate_mobject() gives the fill triangles of a VMobject with upstream's texture coordinates and modes.

  • affects_shader_info_id(func) and triggers_refreshed_triangulation(func) are upstream's decorators as functions: they wrap a method func(self, ...).

  • OpenGLRenderer() renders scenes as upstream's renderer: it clears its framebuffer to the background color, sets the perspective uniforms from the camera (refresh_perspective_uniforms()) and draws each mobject. The shader wrappers of a mobject are drawn by a grid camera that places points as upstream's shaders do (rotated by camera_rotation, scaled by focal_distance / (focal_distance - z), fixed in frame mobjects in the default frame) and lights them with upstream's add_light(), once per mobject rather than per pixel. An OpenGLSurface runs upstream's surface shader instead, and an OpenGLTexturedSurface its textured_surface shader (nearest texel): their triangles are rasterized at pixel centers, lit per pixel, and with depth_test (on by default) tested against and written to the framebuffer's depth buffer. config$renderer = "opengl" makes scenes use it. get_frame() gives a nativeRaster; get_raw_frame_buffer_object_data() the pixels bottom row first, as OpenGL reads them.

  • render_opengl_vectorized_mobject_fill(), render_opengl_vectorized_mobject_stroke() and their _with_matrix helpers build upstream's vertex buffers and uniforms and draw them as upstream's projection shaders do (with config$use_projection_fill_shaders and config$use_projection_stroke_shaders): the fill keeps the part of each triangle on the side of its curve given by its texture mode, and the stroke the points within 0.004 * width of its curve.

  • OpenGLSoftwareContext() stands for moderngl's context: framebuffer(), buffer() and simple_vertex_array(), whose render() draws the vectorized_mobject_fill and vectorized_mobject_stroke shaders. Other GLSL code, as a Mesh's, is not run.

  • Window(renderer) is the window of a live preview: an R graphics device (an interactive session is needed) that shows the renderer's frame on swap_buffers(); handle_event() waits for a mouse or key event in it and passes it to the scene's handlers, on devices that report events (X11 and Windows). Its size follows config$window_size and its position config$window_position on the monitor, which is getOption("manimR.monitor") (a list of x, y, width and height) or 1920 by 1080 pixels at the origin.

Examples

cam <- OpenGLCamera()
cam$set_euler_angles(theta = PI / 4, phi = PI / 3)
round(cam$inverse_rotation_matrix, 3)
#>        [,1]   [,2]  [,3]
#> [1,]  0.707  0.707 0.000
#> [2,] -0.354  0.354 0.866
#> [3,]  0.612 -0.612 0.500
cam$get_position()
#> [1]  0  0 11
tri <- triangulate_mobject(OpenGLSquare())
length(tri)
#> [1] 42
s <- Shader(name = "surface")
names(s$shader_program)
#> [1] "fragment_shader" "vertex_shader"  
# \donttest{
r <- OpenGLRenderer()
scene <- Scene$new(renderer = r)
scene$add(OpenGLCircle()$set_fill(RED, 1))
r$update_frame(scene)
dim(r$get_raw_frame_buffer_object_data())
#> [1] 1080 1920    4
r$close_device()
# }
